extracted.intended_audience: applicants for NIH/NIGMS NRSA Individual Postdoctoral Fellowship (F32)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluation standards for preparing, submitting, and managing an NRSA Individual Postdoctoral Fellowship (F32) application to NIGMS, and how applications are reviewed and administered after award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application receipt deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications must be submitted by fixed receipt dates: April 8, August 8, and December 8 (or the next workday if on a weekend/holiday).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications submitted after these dates will not be accepted. See NIH standard due dates for submission schedule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Earliest award start timing and activation window
rubrics_metrics.description: Earliest award start dates correspond to receipt dates (April: earliest Dec start; August: earliest Apr start; December: earliest Jul start). Once awarded, fellows have 6 months to activate (start) the fellowship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Activation must occur within 6 months of the Notice of Research Fellowship Award; activation cannot occur between October 1 and November 15. If you cannot activate within 6 months, request an extension with a signed letter explaining circumstances; approval issues a revised NoA with new latest activation date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of current application forms and NOFO
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must use the most recent NIH forms and follow the F32 Notice of Funding Opportunity (NOFO) and SF424 Application Guide instructions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check the NIH unsolicited application and forms webpages for current forms and NOFO details before preparing your application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinction between F32 (postdoc) and F33 (senior) fellowships
rubrics_metrics.description: F32 supports mentored postdoctoral research training to develop into independent researchers; F33 supports experienced scientists (≥7 years postdoctoral experience) for sabbatical/major career changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose the award type appropriate to your career stage; F33 targets independent investigators and sabbatical-type training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citizenship/permanent residency eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: By the time of award, fellows must be U.S. citizens, non-citizen nationals, or lawful permanent residents (valid I-551 or equivalent legal verification).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grants management specialists may request notarized proof of permanent residency prior to award issuance; provide required documentation promptly to avoid delays.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terminal degree requirement before activation
rubrics_metrics.description: Before a postdoctoral fellowship award can be activated, the individual must have received an accepted doctoral-equivalent degree (PhD, MD, DO, DDS, DVM, etc.) from an accredited domestic or foreign institution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If degree completion is pending at award, provide certification from the degree-granting institution that all requirements have been met; acceptable documents include signed certification form, diploma specifying degree, or official transcript.

rubrics_metrics.name: Candidate must identify sponsor(s) before submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Before submitting, the candidate must identify a sponsor(s) who will supervise the mentored training experience; more than one sponsor (a sponsor team) is encouraged if advantageous.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When using a sponsor team, identify one individual as the primary sponsor. Sponsors should review and discuss the Research Training Plan with the candidate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Addressing gaps in CV
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants should explain gaps in the candidate section or the biosketch personal statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide concise, clear explanations in the candidate section or personal statement so reviewers can evaluate the record appropriately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and research product citation limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: In the biosketch personal statement, candidates may cite up to four publications or research products that highlight experience and qualifications for the project. Research products include a broad set of artifacts (conference abstracts, posters, patents, data, curricula, protocols, software, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hyperlinks/URLs are not allowed. Interim research products have specific citation requirements—see Interim Research Product FAQs for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriateness of applying when postdoc research overlaps graduate research
rubrics_metrics.description: NRSA fellowships are for training; training potential is a key criterion. Applicants doing similar work to graduate studies should emphasize acquisition of new skills, techniques, systems, or new aspects of the organism that justify the fellowship as new training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly describe opportunities for new training and how they relate to long-term career goals to demonstrate training potential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time in sponsor's lab considered for funding decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: NIGMS considers time already spent in the sponsor's laboratory; applicants who have been in the current sponsor's lab for >2 years at submission may not be considered for funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss extenuating circumstances with program staff before submitting if you have long tenure in the sponsor's lab; exceptions may be considered for competitive applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Justification required for second postdoc in a new lab
rubrics_metrics.description: If applying for a second postdoc in a new lab, you must justify how the new research relates to prior postdoc work and career goals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly explain how the second postdoc adds distinct training benefits and furthers career advancement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility for foreign research
rubrics_metrics.description: Fellowships for postdoctoral research in foreign countries are allowed only if no U.S. laboratory does comparable research or the foreign lab has unique resources not available in comparable U.S. labs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a strong rationale in the application; be aware award processing may take extra time for stipend and allowance payment arrangements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Candidate authors Research Training Plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Candidates are expected to write the Research Training Plan; the sponsor should review and discuss it in detail with the applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fellowship Research Training Plans do not require the extensive experimental detail of regular research grants, but must be fundamentally sound and tailored to training needs. Review by other knowledgeable colleagues is recommended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Division of responsibilities between candidate and sponsor
rubrics_metrics.description: The NOFO and SF424 Application Guide specify which sections of the application are the responsibility of the Candidate or the Sponsor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult the NOFO and SF424 Application Guide for exact responsibilities when assembling the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference letter selection and submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants should follow NIH guidance on selecting referees, provide instructions to referees, and follow the reference letter submission process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Visit NIH webpages on reference letters for details. For resubmissions, new reference letters must be obtained; reviewers will not have access to prior letters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sponsor must demonstrate commitment to tailored training
rubrics_metrics.description: Regardless of career stage, the primary sponsor must demonstrate commitment to ensuring the candidate receives tailored training facilitating skills development and career advancement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the sponsor has limited postdoc training experience, explain how training will be ensured, possibly via a sponsor team with one identified primary sponsor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required content of the Research Training Plan
rubrics_metrics.description: The Research Training Plan should relate the proposed research to the candidate's career goals, explain the relationship between the candidate's research and the sponsor's ongoing program, be tailored to the candidate's experience level, and allow development of necessary skills for career advancement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Section IV of the NOFO and the SF424 Application Guide for detailed expectations. Make training-specific elements explicit and aligned with career objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement for Responsible Conduct of Research (RCR) plan
rubrics_metrics.description: All fellowship applicants must include a plan to obtain instruction in the responsible conduct of research that documents prior RCR instruction and proposes future instruction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The plan must address five instructional components: format, subject matter, faculty participation, duration, and frequency, and describe the sponsor/mentor's role. Applications lacking an RCR plan will be considered incomplete and may be delayed. See NIH policy notices NOT-OD-10-019 and NOT-OD-22-055 for full requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resubmission policy and expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Resubmissions are allowed per the NOFO and submission policies in most cases. Applicants should address reviewer concerns and describe progress since the prior version.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Update publication lists and sponsor information if necessary. New reference letters and appendix materials must be supplied for resubmissions because reviewers won't have access to prior letters/materials. Observe receipt deadlines for resubmissions (April 8, August 8, December 8).

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-submission review timeline
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH review for fellowship applications can take between 8 and 20 months after the due date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Receipt/Review/Potential Start date mapping is provided (e.g., April 8 receipt -> study section review Jun/Jul -> potential Dec start). Contact the Scientific Review Officer (SRO) for questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: How applications are reviewed and revised fellowship review criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Revised fellowship review criteria (effective for receipt dates on/after Jan 25, 2025) are intended to help reviewers evaluate a candidate's potential and the quality of their research training plan without undue influence of sponsor/institution reputation, aligning review information to the candidate's training needs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The revised peer review criteria apply to activity codes F30, F31, F32, F33, F99/K00. See 'Changes to the Fellowship Review Criteria' for full details of how criteria are restructured.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority score calculation and score reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Priority score is determined by calculating the mean of study section members' impact scores (1-9) for the application and multiplying the average by 10, yielding a possible range of 10 (best) to 90 (worst).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The overall priority score is not an average of the individual criterion scores. Within one week of the study section meeting, the priority score is typically available via eRA Commons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary statement contents
rubrics_metrics.description: The SRO prepares a summary statement that becomes the official IC record and contains the overall resume and summary of review discussion, written critiques by assigned reviewers including scores for the five main review criteria, overall impact score and percentile (if discussed), study section recommendations, budget recommendations, and administrative notes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The summary statement is available in eRA Commons about 4–6 weeks after the study section meets. Contact your program officer with questions after receiving the summary statement.

rubrics_metrics.name: How funding decisions and award notifications are made
rubrics_metrics.description: The Notice of Award (NoA) is the official notification emailed to the grantee organization with a copy to the PD/PI; program officers may give informal notice, but NoA is official. When NIH issues the NoA it is available in eRA Commons Status module.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program officers may contact PIs informally about likely funding; however, only the NoA is the official documentation of award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination of fellowship term (duration)
rubrics_metrics.description: The term of a fellowship (length) is influenced by the study section recommendation, prior NRSA postdoctoral support (total NRSA postdoctoral support cannot exceed 3 years), and other factors; the study section may recommend a shorter term than requested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If offered a shorter term, consult your program director. NRSA postdoctoral support is capped by Congress at 3 years total for typical cases; adjustments are made if prior NRSA support exists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stipend level determination
rubrics_metrics.description: Stipend levels are set by HHS/NRSA and vary by stipend level (0–7); your stipend level is determined by the amount of time spent doing biomedical research-related activities since you earned your first terminal degree.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you earned two terminal degrees, stipend is calculated from the date of the first degree. Your stipend level in year 1 is the level for which you were eligible when offered the fellowship, even if eligibility changes before activation. Stipends increase by one level each funded year; FY stipend values are published in NIH notices (e.g., NOT-OD-24-104).

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementation of stipend
rubrics_metrics.description: Institutions or sponsors may supplement fellow stipends if supplemental funds come from a non-Federal source and are provided without any additional obligation from the fellow.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure supplements are lawful and do not impose additional obligations on the fellow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tax treatment of stipends
rubrics_metrics.description: Stipends are taxable; in most cases the business office will issue IRS Form 1099 for fellows to use when filing taxes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult institutional payroll/grants management for tax reporting details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional allowance usage and no carryover
rubrics_metrics.description: Institutional allowance is awarded to help support training costs; there is no carryover of institutional allowance funds from one budget period to the next.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All institutional allowance funds must be spent in the budget year in which they were awarded; see NIH Grants Policy Statement for specific allowance levels and permissible uses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict with other pending fellowships or offers
rubrics_metrics.description: If you have other fellowship applications pending you must withdraw them before accepting an NRSA fellowship. If you accept another fellowship and later decide you want the NRSA, follow withdrawal and communications procedures with your program director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program directors will ask for copies of withdrawal letters. If you have competing offers, discuss timing and probabilities with your program director before accepting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure to withdraw an NRSA application or accept another offer
rubrics_metrics.description: To withdraw an application, send a letter to your assigned NIGMS program director countersigned by an authorized institutional representative requesting withdrawal; scan/upload and email as PDF to the program director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow 'Withdraw Your Application' guidance on Grants & Funding for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Activation paperwork requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: To activate the fellowship, submit an Activation Notice (PHS 416-5) before funding disbursement; fellows with <12 months prior NRSA postdoctoral support must complete a Payback Agreement (PHS 6031).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Completed PDF forms with digital signatures must be emailed from an Authorized Organization Representative to the Grants Management Specialist named in Section 9 of the NoA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payback obligation rules
rubrics_metrics.description: For every month of NRSA postdoctoral support (up to 12 months) you incur an obligation to pay back that support; one month of payback is required for every month in which you incur payback obligation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You can fulfill payback by continuing fellowship support for 12 additional months or by doing biomedical research-related activities while not supported by the fellowship. See GPS sections on reporting and payback for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requests for additional childcare funds
rubrics_metrics.description: NRSA fellowship awardees are eligible to request additional funds for childcare costs provided by a licensed provider.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests can be made at application, as just-in-time before award, in the annual progress report, or mid-budget as an administrative supplement; consult FAQs and the Grants Management Specialist on the NoA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual progress report requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Fellows must submit annual progress reports at the end of every funded year except the last; reports are due 2 months before the next year of support. The institution submits the report, but the candidate writes the narrative; the sponsor provides a written evaluation of accomplishments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a report is late, contact your program director immediately. Missing a progress report when funding expires will delay the next year of funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget carryover and unspent institutional allowance
rubrics_metrics.description: Unspent institutional allowance from year 1 cannot be spent in year 2; there is no carryover.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan budget expenditures accordingly; consult institutional grants office for allowable uses in the budget year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Change in scope and NIH prior approval
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients may make changes in methodology, approach, or other aspects of project objectives, but changes that constitute a change in scope (direction, aims, objectives, purposes, or type of research training) require prior approval from the NIH awarding IC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The recipient should make an initial determination of significance of change and consult with the Grants Management Officer as necessary. See GPS 8.1.2.5 for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retaining fellowship after changes in project/sponsor/institution
rubrics_metrics.description: If you change projects, sponsors, AND institution, you cannot keep the fellowship. If you change only one of the three (project OR sponsor OR institution), you can request permission to retain the fellowship. If you change two of the three parameters, approval from the program director and NIGMS TWD leadership is required and will be granted only for very compelling justification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests to retain fellowship after changes must be discussed with and approved by program staff; fellowship transfers are restricted between Oct 1 and Nov 15.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transferring fellowship mid-year when sponsor moves
rubrics_metrics.description: A fellowship can be transferred mid-year if the sponsor moves, but the process may take several weeks because stipend and institutional allowance funds must be transferred between institutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notify program director and grants management specialist early to expedite the transfer; administrative timelines vary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leave of absence rules and approval
rubrics_metrics.description: Extended leaves (>15 calendar days sick or >60 calendar days parental) require NIH awarding IC approval via a letter signed by fellow, sponsor, and institutional official submitted by AOR. Award funds cannot be spent during unpaid leave; health insurance continuation may be allowed per institutional policy. The award is extended to compensate for approved leave time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests must specify dates and be emailed to the named Grants Management Specialist. Fellowship cannot be re-started between Oct 1 and Nov 15.

rubrics_metrics.name: Termination procedures and institutional allowance penalty
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon termination you must submit a termination notice (PHS 416-7 via xTrain) within 30 days. If you terminate within the first 6 months of a fellowship year, the institutional allowance will be reduced by half; otherwise there is generally no penalty if payback obligation is satisfied or will be fulfilled in the new position.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow xTrain submission instructions and notify NIH promptly to avoid administrative issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension policy beyond the Congressionally mandated 3-year NRSA limit
rubrics_metrics.description: NRSA postdoctoral support is subject to a 3-year Congressional limit. Generally, requests for extensions are not considered, though in unusual circumstances a 6-month extension may be considered for substantial new training; very rare 12-month extensions require approval from NIGMS TWD leadership and program director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extensions cannot be requested to finish originally proposed experiments or manuscripts. Contact program director to discuss eligibility and justification before requesting an extension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Where to find forms and policy references
rubrics_metrics.description: Activation, payback, and other forms (e.g., PHS 416-5, PHS 6031, PHS 416-7) and policy notices are available via NIH grants/forms webpages and specific NOT-OD notices referenced on the page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the links provided in the NOFO/SF424 guides and NIH Grants & Funding web pages to obtain current forms and policy documents (e.g., NOT-OD-10-019, NOT-OD-22-055, NOT-OD-24-104, NOT-OD-24-116).

rubrics_metrics.name: Who to contact before review or to provide updates
rubrics_metrics.description: Contact the Scientific Review Officer (SRO) who oversees the study section for questions about the review process or to submit an update; SRO contact info is available in eRA Commons about a month after submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Find SRO details via your eRA Commons account and NIH staff role pages; for programmatic questions contact your program director listed on the summary statement once available.
